questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (4.2,0);\coordinate (A) at (2.1,3.94953);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$4.2\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\pic[draw,"$62^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.95cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The end of an A-frame tent is $4.2$ m wide and each sloping side makes $62^{\circ}$ with the ground.
Find the height of the tent at its centre, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Used the full width of $4.2$ m instead of halving it to get the base of the right-angled triangle.
Divided by $\tan62^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying, treating the height as the denominator.
Used $\cos62^{\circ}$, which gives the sloping side rather than the height.

questions.solution_text:
The height splits the tent into two right-angled triangles, each with a base of $2.1$ m.
$\tan62^{\circ}=\frac{h}{2.1}$
$h=2.1\tan62^{\circ}$
$=3.9495\ldots$
$\approx3.95\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.5]\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (9.0,0);\coordinate (D) at (4.5,0);\coordinate (A) at (4.5,3.4);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$9.0\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\draw[dashed] (A)--(D) node[midway,right] {$3.4\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.5cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.5cm!(A)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=1.5cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A gable end is $9.0$ m wide and its ridge is $3.4$ m above the wall top.
Find $\theta$, the angle each rafter makes with the horizontal, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used the full width of $9.0$ m as the base instead of halving it.
Swapped the height and the half-width, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4.5}{3.4}\right)$.
Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating the $4.5$ m half-width as the length of the rafter.

questions.solution_text:
Half of the gable is a right-angled triangle with a base of $4.5$ m and a height of $3.4$ m.
$\tan\theta=\frac{3.4}{4.5}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4}{4.5}\right)$
$=37.0730\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx37^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
A bridge truss has a vertical post $CD$ from its apex $C$ to the horizontal deck $AB$, with $D$ between $A$ and $B$. The left chord $AC$ is $10$ m long, $\angle CAB=30^{\circ}$ and $\angle CBA=45^{\circ}$.
Find $DB$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Used the $10$ m chord as the shared height instead of first calculating $CD$.
Used $10\cos30^{\circ}$ for the shared height instead of $10\sin30^{\circ}$.
Calculated the right-hand hypotenuse $BC=5/\sin45^{\circ}$ instead of the horizontal distance $DB$.

questions.solution_text:
First find the shared post.
$CD=10\sin30^{\circ}=5\text{ m}$.
In the right-hand triangle, $\tan45^{\circ}=\frac{5}{DB}$.
$DB=\frac{5}{\tan45^{\circ}}=5\text{ m}$.
$DB=5.00\text{ m}$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.42]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (D) at (3.33436,0);\coordinate (B) at (10.83436,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.33436,3.45283);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,above left] {$4.8\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(B);\draw (C)--(D);\draw (D)--(B) node[midway,below] {$7.5\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.6cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.6cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$46^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.6cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=B--A--C};\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.75cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=C--B--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A gable end has an off-centre ridge on a vertical post.
The left rafter is $4.8$ m long and rises at $46^{\circ}$, and the foot of the post is $7.5$ m from the right-hand wall.
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Swapped the post and the $7.5$ m run, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7.5}{3.45}\right)$.
Used the $4.8$ m rafter itself as the height of the post instead of finding the post first.
Used $\cos46^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin46^{\circ}$ when finding the post.

questions.solution_text:
First find the post, the side the two triangles share.
$\sin46^{\circ}=\frac{h}{4.8}$
$h=4.8\sin46^{\circ}$
$=3.4528\ldots\text{ m}$
Now use $h$ in the right-hand triangle.
$\tan\theta=\frac{3.4528\ldots}{7.5}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4528\ldots}{7.5}\right)$
$=24.7203\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx25^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
A triangular truss has a perpendicular altitude of $3$ m whose foot lies between the ends of its horizontal base. Its sloping sides make angles of $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ with the base.
Find the perimeter of the triangle, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Added only the two horizontal base sections and omitted both sloping sides.
Added only the two sloping sides and omitted the horizontal base.
Used twice the correct base length, counting each horizontal section twice.

questions.solution_text:
The altitude divides the triangle into two right-angled triangles.
Base $=\frac{3}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{3}{\tan60^{\circ}}=6.9282\ldots\text{ m}$.
Sloping sides $=\frac{3}{\sin30^{\circ}}+\frac{3}{\sin60^{\circ}}=9.4641\ldots\text{ m}$.
Perimeter $=\frac{3}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{3}{\tan60^{\circ}}+\frac{3}{\sin30^{\circ}}+\frac{3}{\sin60^{\circ}}$.
Perimeter $=16.3923\ldots\text{ m}\approx16.39\text{ m}$.

questions.question_text:
A tree snaps and its top touches the ground. The remaining section and the fallen section are perpendicular. The ground distance from the base of the tree to its fallen top is $12$ m. The remaining section is inclined at $30^{\circ}$ to horizontal ground.
Find the height of the original tree, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Calculated only the fallen section using $12\sin30^{\circ}$ and omitted the remaining section.
Calculated only the remaining section using $12\cos30^{\circ}$ and omitted the fallen section.
Added the $12$ m ground distance to the two tree sections, calculating the triangle's perimeter instead of the original tree height.

questions.solution_text:
The ground distance is the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle formed by the two tree sections.
Remaining section $=12\cos30^{\circ}=10.3923\ldots\text{ m}$.
Fallen section $=12\sin30^{\circ}=6\text{ m}$.
Original height $=12\cos30^{\circ}+12\sin30^{\circ}=16.3923\ldots\text{ m}$.
The original tree was $16.4\text{ m}$ high.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (P) at (0,0);\coordinate (Q) at (3.19094,0);\coordinate (S) at (0.84547,1.35304);\coordinate (U) at (2.34547,1.35304);\draw (-0.7,0)--(P);\draw (Q)--(3.89,0);\draw[dashed] (P)--(Q);\draw[very thick] (P)--(S) node[midway,above left] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (Q)--(U) node[midway,above right] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (S)--(U) node[midway,above] {$12\text{ m}$};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=Q--P--S};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=U--Q--P};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A lifting bridge has two identical sections, each $x$ m long, hinged at opposite banks.
Lowered, they exactly span the river.
Raised to $58^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, their tips are $12$ m apart.
Find the width of the river, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found $x$, the length of one section, and stopped instead of doubling it for the river.
Divided the $12$ m gap by $\cos58^{\circ}$ rather than by $1-\cos58^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Lowered, the sections span the river, so the river is $2x$ m wide.
Raised, each section covers a horizontal distance of $x\cos58^{\circ}$, and what is left over is the gap.
$2x-2x\cos58^{\circ}=12$
$2x(1-\cos58^{\circ})=12$
$2x=\frac{12}{1-\cos58^{\circ}}$
$=25.5275\ldots$
$\approx25.5\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
From the ends of a straight horizontal road $8$ m long, a balloon directly above a point between the ends is observed at angles of elevation of $45^{\circ}$ from both ends.
Find the height of the balloon above the road, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Used the full road length as the base of one right-angled triangle instead of accounting for both horizontal distances.
Halved the road twice, using a horizontal distance of $2$ m instead of $4$ m.

questions.solution_text:
Draw a vertical from the balloon to the road. Let its height be $h$ and the two horizontal distances be $p$ and $q$.
$p=\frac{h}{\tan45^{\circ}}$ and $q=\frac{h}{\tan45^{\circ}}$.
Since $p+q=8$, $\frac{h}{\tan45^{\circ}}+\frac{h}{\tan45^{\circ}}=8$.
$2h=8$, so $h=4\text{ m}$.
The height is $4.00\text{ m}$.
